A follow-up to our 9th place in the BEHAVIOR Challenge 2026: as promised, we open-sourced everything, and our team received the Open Source Prize 🏆

Our solution is one VLA policy for all 100 household tasks (39.2%), plus a GPT-6 Astra coding agent that practices on training instances and takes over the hardest tasks (44.6% in total).

It was also great to see that many teams this year, including the top two, built on our open-source solution from last year. That's exactly why we share our work.

posts.description:
Saw a post similar to a project I’ve been working on, so I wanted to share.

CourtVision turns a single-camera NBA broadcast into possessions, makes and misses, rebounds and a box score, running locally on a Mac.

How it works:
• Detection: a ResNet-18 CenterNet distilled from RF-DETR looks at 3 frames at once, so a blurred ball still stands out. It runs on Apple’s Neural Engine.
• Court mapping: A broadcast camera only pans, tilts and zooms, so those are the only things it fits per frame.
• Events: a rules engine turns the tracks into possessions, shots and rebounds. A small rim CNN re-judges every make or miss 2.5 s later.
• Decision layer: Jev calls the play type, how big the moment is, and whether each line of Claude’s commentary is backed by the facts. Each call has a deadline of 1.5 s or less and a rule-based fallback.
Live vs recorded:
• Live: 21–30 fps against a 30 fps broadcast on an M3 Pro. Working towards getting it to live level, could probably do it with more compute.
• Recorded: decides possession over the whole game at once, and gets the team with the ball right 97% of the time on held-out footage. The model has only been trained on ~42 games, a few shorter clips.

Code: https://lnkd.in/gcC_J4Da
(Note: have't worked on this in a bit, open to improvements)

posts.description:
Noetic Hack is back, and this time we're taking AI builders to COP31 Türkiye 🌍

With ATOX, we're running AI for Climate, an online hackathon where you spend a weekend building an AI prototype for a real climate problem. Selected teams present at the GAUC Pavilion during COP31, the United Nations climate summit in Antalya, and meet climate experts and potential partners there.

You don't need a climate background. If you build with AI, this is a good weekend to find out whether climate is a problem you want to keep working on.

The kind of questions teams are tackling:
• Forecasting tomorrow's solar and wind output well enough for the grid to plan around it
• Spotting methane leaks or illegal logging from satellite images
• Predicting which streets will flood in the next storm and warning residents in time
• Flagging claims in sustainability reports that don't hold up

12 Nov: Lightning pitches
13 Nov: Teams finalised
14–15 Nov: Online build, mentor feedback and demos
18 Nov: Selected teams present at COP31

Apply solo or as a team of 4 to 6 by 13 Nov:

🌐: https://luma.com/ag12jspz

Applying from London? Join our London hub social on Fri 13 Nov, 6 to 9pm, to meet other London hackers and form your team before the build. Climate tech folks are welcome too.

Limited spots:
‼️: https://lnkd.in/epNxFk9p

#AIforClimate #COP31 #ClimateTech #Hackathon

posts.description:
Was chatting with Joanna Braunold from my team today about how our brains work in mysterious ways.

The exact moments my mind decides to produce absolute genius, or just figure out the exact next tasks I should actually be working on:
❌ During a 2-hour brainstorming meeting.
❌ Staring blankly at a laptop with a triple espresso.
✔️ 2 minutes into a hot shower with shampoo in my eyes.

The problem? By the time I turn off the water, grab a towel, and find my phone, that insight has evaporated into thin air, leaving me with nothing but a faint scent of lavender and regret.

Forget sending people to Mars, Elon. We need the waterproof Grok Bot Shower Button™️ next to the loofah. Modern problems require wet-fingered solutions.
Let us dictate our shower thoughts before they go down the drain! 🚿💡
(Attached: A preview of the only upgrade my bathroom actually needs 👇, generated by Gemini - I love Agents Collaboration 😊 )

However, this does mean that I am actively looking for a team and project to bring my talents to. I'm super passionate about anything Systems or Cybersecurity (that's you GCP), and would love to chat or connect if you're looking for interns!

(giggles for engagement)

Last Saturday, I went to an NVIDIA warm-up event for GTC Berlin and drank beer brewed by AI agents. 🦞🍺

Gerhard runs Lobster Lager. Agents built his website and handle the logistics, the ingredients, the recipes and the brewing. What they still haven't automated: taxes. Very German.

His line stuck with me: "If I, at 68, can use this, imagine what you could be doing."

As a DevRel, I was just as hooked on how Mark Heaps ran the room. He turned every transition into a story, brought a bit of Texas to Berlin, and never pitched once. He put builders on stage and let them do the inspiring. Honestly, a masterclass in developer storytelling.

Want to build something yourself? Here are some free resources from the event:
